summary: Initial discovery for embeddings + reranking pipeline. PioneerSearch is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private Redwood deployments. Key concerns: throughput at 1000+ qps, vector dimensionality (512 vs 768), hybrid search with keyword filters, vector DB integration and migration effort, security (VPC, KMS, SOC2) and benchmarking plan.
topics: Current search stack and pain points
Vector DB integration and connector patterns
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-17 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Gupta (Redwood SE); Liam O'Connor (Pioneer), Priya Patel (ML Eng), Marcus Li (Data Eng)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro: I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, and this is Samira on the SE side. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Liam (Pioneer): Good, thanks. Hey Alex, Samira. we have about 45 minutes, want to run through what we're trying to do and get a sense of deployment options.
[00:14] Alex (Redwood): Perfect. could you give us a quick overview of current stack and what you're looking to improve?
[00:20] Liam (Pioneer): Sure. Our current search is Elastic for inverted index + a custom rerank model that uses embeddings computed offline. It's slow for near real-time content and costs are creeping up. We're exploring full embeddings-first retrieval with a vector DB + a lightweight reranker. Need to understand throughput, cost, and how Redwood would fit.
[00:37] Priya (Pioneer): yea, and also dimensionality question — our current embeddings are 768 dims from an open model; we've been experimenting with 512 via quantized models to cut cost. Curious how that affects recall and rerank.
[00:50] Samira (Redwood): got it. Typical conversation. At a high level Redwood can serve embeddings and rerank in multiple ways — Hosted API for quick start, Dedicated for predictable qps and lower unit cost, or Private for VPC/on-prem for strict data policies. For vector DB integration we see two patterns: Redwood as the embeddings/rerank runtime calling your vector DB (e.g., Pinecone, Milvus) or Redwood hosting the vector index directly in Dedicated/private via our integrated store or via connectors.
[01:12] Marcus (Pioneer): connector approach—what does that look like? Are we rewriting ingestion pipelines?
[01:18] Samira (Redwood): usually we provide ingestion SDKs and a connector that can push vectors to your DB. For a migration we can either (a) compute embeddings in Redwood and push to your DB, or (b) bulk import your existing embeddings. minimal pipeline changes in both cases. there can be some mapping work for metadata, filters, and hybrid search keys.
[01:38] Liam (Pioneer): hybrid search — we want BM25 for some queries and embedding retrieval for others; then rerank top-K. latency target is sub-200ms p95 for user-facing search, throughput 800-1200 qps during peak. is that feasible?
[01:56] Samira (Redwood): sub-200ms p95 at 1k qps is challenging for hosted unless you use aggressive caching and shorter sequences; Dedicated with reserved gpus is the sweet spot for consistent latency. We can hit ~150-200ms p95 with Dedicated and batching tuned, plus prefix / KV cache for repeated session queries. For Hosted we can often achieve ~250-300ms with our low-latency tiers.
[02:24] Priya (Pioneer): what about embedding dimensionality tradeoffs? 768 -> 512 quantized — do we lose recall?
[02:31] Samira (Redwood): depends on your data and model. 512 often is fine for many corpora and gives 30-40% memory/cost savings. If you're doing rerank downstream, small drops in retrieval recall can be recovered by a stronger reranker. we recommend running an A/B with your eval set. Samira: we'll share recommended eval prompts.
[02:52] Marcus (Pioneer): index size — we've got ~120M docs, average 1 vector per doc. That's big. What's the storage + query cost estimate?
[03:01] Alex (Redwood): for 120M at 768 dims that's sizable; storage depends on quantization (8-bit vs 4-bit). On Dedicated you get more control: you can use product quantization and sharding strategies. We can send a back-of-envelope. Also if you keep stems in your existing Elastic for hybrid filters you can reduce vector space by storing only candidates.
[03:24] Liam (Pioneer): security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, VPC peering, and KMS integration. Any red flags?
[03:33] Alex (Redwood): Redwood is SOC2 Type II, supports SAML SSO, full audit logs in Redwood Console, VPC peering for Private and Dedicated, and KMS/HSM support for Private deployments. Hosted can use customer-managed keys via KMS in some regions, but Private is the best fit for locked-down requirements.
[03:51] Priya (Pioneer): for the Dedicated option, how does failover and graceful degradation work? Say one shard is slow — will traffic fall back to a hosted model?
[03:59] Samira (Redwood): yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants or to Hosted for non-sensitive traffic. You can set policies: region, latency, cost. For Dedicated we recommend canary pods and multi-AZ.
[04:13] Marcus (Pioneer): do you support hybrid search natively or do we run our BM25 separately?
[04:18] Samira (Redwood): we have two patterns: do BM25 in your Elastic and call Redwood for vector rerank, or use Redwood's hybrid layer which can combine sparse and dense signals — hybrid search in the runtime. The runtime accepts sparse keys and does rerank on top-K candidates.
[04:33] Liam (Pioneer): curious about throughput testing — can we run a 1k qps benchmark with our dataset? what's the typical runbook?
[04:40] Alex (Redwood): absolutely. Samira will share a benchmark template. We do a staged benchmark: seed data ingestion, warmup (KV cache), then steady-state qps sweep. For Dedicated we can provision capacity for the test; for Hosted we often run synthetic loads but will discuss rate limits.
[04:58] Priya (Pioneer): any limits on vector dimensionality? and embedding models supported?
[05:03] Samira (Redwood): we support typical sizes (128, 256, 512, 768, 1024). Model compatibility: any model that outputs fixed-size vectors; we have optimized kernels for common open models. If you're using custom models, we can onboard them — may need model artifacts and some perf testing.
[05:22] Liam (Pioneer): cost model — how do you price embeddings + rerank at scale? token? vector ops?
[05:29] Alex (Redwood): Hosted pricing is usage-based per-embedding compute and per-rerank request; Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit — lower per-unit compute and storage; Private is license + infra. We'll send a decision matrix and sample TCO for your 120M corpus.
[05:45] Marcus (Pioneer): what about vector DB lock-in — if we use Redwood's integrated store is migration easy?
[05:51] Samira (Redwood): yes, we support export tools and standard formats (FAISS, Annoy, flat files) and connectors to export to Pinecone/Milvus/Elastic ANN. Avoiding lock-in is a design goal.
[06:04] Liam (Pioneer): integration time — realistic timeline for pilot?
[06:09] Samira (Redwood): typical pilot 4-6 weeks: week 1 ingest and index small slice, week 2 run evals and tuning, week 3 perf benchmarks, week 4 finalize pilot report and recommend deployment. If you go Dedicated there's procurement lead time.
[06:23] Priya (Pioneer): procurement — legal asks around data residency in EU and logging retention. We are EU-based customers with some US operations.
[06:31] Alex (Redwood): we have EU regions and Private for on-prem. Logging retention and redaction policies can be configured. We'll attach SOC2 and data residency docs.
[06:42] Liam (Pioneer): quick Q — does Redwood do rerank tokenization or do we ship model endpoints?
[06:47] Samira (Redwood): rerank can be served as a lightweight model in the runtime; we support function calls and structured outputs. Tokenization is handled server-side; you can also host your own model and call it from Redwood if you need custom infra.
[06:59] Marcus (Pioneer): small tangent — what about KV cache warmup strategies?
[07:02] Samira (Redwood): we do prefix caching and allow pre-warming with a seeded query set. Warmup can drastically reduce cold-start p95.
[07:11] Liam (Pioneer): perfect. Any dealbreakers?
[07:13] Alex (Redwood): none apparent; main decisions are Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private based on latency and compliance. We'll send detailed cost and deployment matrix.
[07:22] Priya (Pioneer): sounds good. Could you include recommended quantization profiles for 512 vs 768?
[07:27] Samira (Redwood): yes — will include expected recall tradeoffs and memory savings.
[07:32] Alex (Redwood): ok let's summarize next steps.
[07:34] Alex (Redwood): Recap: Alex to send pricing + deployment comparison, Samira to share benchmark template and quantization guidance, Pioneer to share sample index stats and confirm EU data residency specifics. We'll schedule a 30-min benchmark kickoff once we have sample data.
[07:50] Liam (Pioneer): thanks everyone. we'll aim to get the sample stats by Friday.
[07:54] Alex (Redwood): great talk soon. bye.

Notes: transcript has occasional imperfect transcriptions (e.g., "SOC two" for SOC2, "Redwood Privat"), filler words kept, minor speaker mislabels present.
